```{r smooth-m-setup, include=FALSE}
study <- "experiments/estimate_intrinsic_m_smooth_v032"
design_result_dir <- file.path(study, "main_summary")
auto_dir <- file.path(study, "auto_m_v034")
result_dir <- file.path(auto_dir, "summary")

validation <- jsonlite::read_json(file.path(auto_dir, "validation.json"))
runs <- read.csv(file.path(result_dir, "auto_runs.csv"))
overall_all <- read.csv(file.path(result_dir, "overall_summary.csv"))
overall <- overall_all[overall_all$method == "auto_adaptive", , drop = FALSE]
conditions <- read.csv(file.path(result_dir, "current_condition_summary.csv"))

stopifnot(
  isTRUE(validation$complete),
  validation$package_version == "0.3.4",
  nrow(runs) == 90L,
  all(runs$status == "success"),
  all(runs$method == "auto_adaptive"),
  sum(runs$warning_count) == 0L,
  nrow(overall) == 1L,
  nrow(conditions) == 9L
)

initial_exact <- sum(runs$selected_initial_M == runs$true_M)
final_exact <- sum(runs$effective_M == runs$true_M)
initial_under <- sum(runs$selected_initial_M < runs$true_M)
initial_over <- sum(runs$selected_initial_M > runs$true_M)
final_under <- sum(runs$effective_M < runs$true_M)
final_over <- sum(runs$effective_M > runs$true_M)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  out.width = "100%",
  fig.align = "center"
)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.path = paste0(
  tools::file_path_sans_ext(knitr::current_input()), "_files/figure-html/"))
options(knitr.graphics.rel_path = FALSE)
```

## Question

How accurately does the current MPCurver automatic-$M$ workflow recover the
number of latent sample orderings when each ordering has one monotone anchor
and all remaining trajectories are smooth and nonmonotone?

We fitted all 90 fixed datasets with **MPCurver 0.3.4** using
`fit_mpcurve(intrinsic_dim = "auto")`. The final effective $M$ is exact in
**`r final_exact`/90 datasets**. The two errors are underestimates in the
hardest $M=5$ settings; there are no final overestimates. Mean feature-partition
ARI is **`r sprintf("%.3f", overall$mean_ARI)`**, and mean matched ordering
recovery is **`r sprintf("%.3f", overall$mean_ordering_recovery)`**.

## Simulation design

Each dataset contains **300 samples and 60 features**, arranged in balanced
groups following **3, 4, or 5 independent latent orderings**. This gives 20,
15, or 12 features per ordering. For sample $i$ and feature $j$,

$$X_{ij}=f_j(t_{i,z_j})+\epsilon_{ij},$$

where $z_j$ identifies the feature's ordering and the latent positions are
independent Uniform$(0,1)$ draws. Within each group, one feature is a monotone
anchor. Every other feature follows a random smooth mixture,

$$f_j(t)=\sum_{k=2}^{4}
\frac{a_{jk}\sin(k\pi t)+b_{jk}\cos(k\pi t)}{k^2},$$

where the coefficients are independent standard normal draws. Retained curves
have derivatives of both signs on a 1,001-point grid, so every non-anchor
trajectory contains at least one change of direction. Each noiseless feature
is centered and scaled to sample variance one.

The variance signal-to-noise ratio is **1, 4, or 16**, with **10 independent
datasets per condition**. The feature groups are balanced, and the simulation
does not include garbage features.

true ordering and each column is an SNR setting. Blue shows the monotone
anchor; orange and purple show two nonmonotone trajectories in the same group.

## Methods

### Automatic dimension initialization

MPCurver 0.3.4 computes a directional nonlinear similarity for every feature
pair. One feature is sorted, and the other is regressed on its normalized rank
with a natural cubic spline having five fixed degrees of freedom. The score is
the proportion of response variance explained; the symmetric similarity is
the larger score from the two directions.

Single-linkage clustering considers cuts with at most eight groups. A cut is
eligible only when every group contains at least two features. Among eligible
cuts, the selected initial $M$ maximizes mean silhouette width. If the selected
group sizes are $d_1,\ldots,d_M$, adaptive EB starts with the global assignment
probabilities

$$p(z_j=m)=d_m/60.$$

The tree cut therefore initializes the number and relative sizes of the
orderings without imposing a hard feature assignment. Adaptive EB may remove
components during fitting.

### Ordering and fitting

Isomap is applied independently within every selected feature group to
initialize its sample ordering. Coordinate-ascent variational inference (CAVI)
then fits 50 position-grid points, a
second-order random-walk prior with `ridge = 0`, adaptive cell-position priors,
estimated feature-specific noise and smoothness, and annealing from temperature
five to one. Convergence requires absolute ELBO change divided by $ND$ below
$10^{-6}$, with at most 10,000 sweeps.

The reported **effective M** is the number of components whose mean posterior
feature-assignment probability exceeds $10^{-12}$. Feature-group recovery uses
the adjusted Rand index (ARI). Ordering recovery matches occupied inferred
orderings one-to-one with the true orderings by absolute Spearman correlation,
allowing reversal; an unmatched true ordering contributes zero.

All results below use MPCurver **0.3.4**, commit
`15f2b0bbe5dfa61cd46da5160b2bc251e75a0475`.

## Recovery of M

The spline-similarity cut selects the true initial $M$ in
**`r initial_exact`/90 datasets**, with **`r initial_under` underestimates** and
**`r initial_over` overestimates**. After adaptive EB, the effective $M$ is
exact in **`r final_exact`/90**, with **`r final_under` underestimates** and
**`r final_over` overestimates**. Figure 4 reports final exact recovery by
condition, Figure 5 compares it with the initial count, and Table 1 gives the
overall totals.

```{r smooth-m-current-recovery, fig.cap="Figure 4. Exact effective-M recovery for MPCurver 0.3.4 automatic-M adaptive fitting. Columns show the generating M. Each point summarizes 10 datasets at the labeled variance SNR; error bars are 95% Wilson intervals."}
knitr::include_graphics(normalizePath(file.path(result_dir, "current_exact_recovery.png")))
```

```{r smooth-m-current-stages, fig.cap="Figure 5. Exact-M recovery at the similarity-cut initialization and after adaptive EB. The initial count is selected by mean silhouette among single-linkage cuts satisfying the minimum cluster size of two; the final count is posterior occupancy after adaptive fitting. Each point summarizes 10 datasets."}
knitr::include_graphics(normalizePath(file.path(result_dir, "current_initial_vs_final.png")))
```

The two final errors occur for true $M=5$: one at SNR 1 and one at SNR 4
(Figure 6). Both fits retain four occupied orderings. All datasets with true $M=3$ or
$M=4$ are recovered exactly at every SNR.

```{r smooth-m-current-distribution, fig.cap="Figure 6. Estimated effective-M distributions from the current package. Panels identify SNR, rows identify the generating M, and columns identify the fitted effective M. Cell labels give counts out of 10 datasets; outlined cells are exact."}
knitr::include_graphics(normalizePath(file.path(result_dir, "current_estimated_M_distribution.png")))
```

## Recovery of the underlying structure

The current fit has mean feature-partition ARI
**`r sprintf("%.3f", overall$mean_ARI)`**. Its mean matched ordering score is
**`r sprintf("%.3f", overall$mean_ordering_recovery)`**. Table 2 lists every condition. Feature grouping is
nearly exact even at SNR 1, whereas estimation of the continuous sample
positions is more sensitive to noise (Figure 7).

```{r smooth-m-current-structure, fig.cap="Figure 7. Structural recovery from MPCurver 0.3.4. The top row shows mean feature-partition ARI; the bottom row shows mean absolute Spearman correlation after one-to-one matching of inferred and true orderings. Each point averages 10 datasets."}
knitr::include_graphics(normalizePath(file.path(result_dir, "current_structural_recovery.png")))
```

```{r smooth-m-current-condition-table}
table <- conditions[, c("true_M", "snr", "datasets", "initial_exact",
  "final_exact", "mean_ARI", "mean_ordering_recovery", "median_seconds")]
names(table) <- c("True M", "SNR", "Datasets", "Initial M exact",
  "Final M exact", "Mean ARI", "Mean ordering score", "Median seconds")
knitr::kable(table, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE,
  caption = "Table 2. Current-package recovery and runtime by simulation condition.")
```

## Runtime and convergence

All **90 current-package fits** converged without fitting warnings. Median
single-thread runtime is **`r sprintf("%.1f", overall$median_seconds)` seconds**
per dataset. Runtime (Figure 11) includes similarity calculation, automatic dimension
selection, ordering initialization, annealing, and adaptive fitting.

```{r smooth-m-current-runtime, fig.cap="Figure 11. Median single-thread runtime of MPCurver 0.3.4 automatic-M adaptive fitting. Each point summarizes 10 complete fits, including similarity calculation, dimension initialization, and adaptive EB."}
knitr::include_graphics(normalizePath(file.path(result_dir, "current_runtime.png")))
```

## Summary and reproduction

On these balanced one-anchor datasets, the current MPCurver workflow recovers
the final effective ordering count in **`r final_exact`/90 datasets** and never
overestimates it. The two misses combine two true orderings in the hardest
$M=5$ settings. Feature groups remain nearly exact overall; continuous ordering
recovery improves sharply with SNR.

This design assumes at least two features per ordering, includes one monotone
anchor in every group, and contains no garbage features. The minimum-cluster
rule prevents singleton orderings but does not identify unstructured features;
that requires a separate background or garbage component.

The [experiment directory](https://github.com/AgueroZZ/InferOrder/tree/master/experiments/estimate_intrinsic_m_smooth_v032/auto_m_v034)
contains all 90 fixed inputs, saved fits, validation records, result tables,
current-package figures, and reproduction scripts. The frozen MPCurver 0.3.4
source archive has SHA-256
`58d0c99c6170994c82eedba190fb1c28a63eb47530c575705323c3cf3992b7c6`.
